title: Shift-change companion and alert-template surface prototype
creator: Marissa Koh
description:
Goal: Design a lightweight 'Shift-change companion' surface in the Redwood Console optimized for fast on‑call transfers and reliable incident continuity. The surface is a compact, persistent drawer available on the Alerts and SLO pages that surfaces current active alerts, SLO deviation snapshot, recommended next steps, and one-click actions: transfer ownership, create a postmortem stub, append quick notes, and send a templated status update.

Scope: prototype designs for desktop, high-fidelity Figma frames for interaction, microcopy for templates, accessibility pass (keyboard + screen reader), and a short usability script for a 5-person usability round. Integrations: quick-links to runbooks (drive/notion), link to GitHub incident issue template, and telemetry hooks for handoff completion metrics.

Out-of-scope: full runbook authoring inside the drawer, mobile-first redesign (desktop only for this ticket), integrations with third-party on-call providers (follow-up ticket).
decisions: Keep the companion as a persistent right-side drawer on Alerts and SLO pages (not modal) to reduce disruption.
Expose only high-value actions by default: Transfer, Create Postmortem, Send Status Update. Secondary actions live under ‘More’ to reduce cognitive load.
Use progressive disclosure for runbook content: show runbook name and last-updated timestamp; deep-link to full runbook in a separate tab.
Use templated status messages with optional variables ({{incident_id}}, {{sla_status}}) to speed cross-team comms.
tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Limiting displayed runbook content reduces immediate context but keeps drawer lightweight; we rely on deep-links for full runbook browsing.
Tradeoff: One-click postmortem stub will seed minimal fields (title, owner, start-time) to encourage creation within the golden hour; more detailed postmortems remain in the postmortem workflow.
Tradeoff: Desktop-only for v1 to accelerate delivery; mobile will be addressed in a follow-up after validating desktop workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with clickable flows for: transfer oncall, create postmortem stub, send templated status update, and link to runbook.
Accessibility checklist completed: keyboard focus, ARIA labels for drawer controls, contrast ratios meet WCAG AA.
Usability: average time to complete a handoff task <= 90s in lab test (5 participants).
Engineering signoff on telemetry hooks and API endpoints required for one-click actions (ENG-7833).
metrics: Primary: Handoff completion rate (percentage of shifts where companion actions used).
Secondary: Time-to-acknowledge after handoff created, Postmortem creation within 1 hour, Number of templated status messages sent per incident.
